questions: Should the array indices be considered 1-based when describing the P_i‑th element, i.e., does P_i = 1 mean insert at the very beginning of the current array?
When inserting the number i, does the existing element that was previously at position P_i shift to position P_i+1, preserving the order of all other elements?
Are the values P_1, P_2, …, P_N guaranteed to satisfy 1 ≤ P_i ≤ i for every i, or must we handle inputs that violate this condition?
If the input contains extra whitespace or line breaks (e.g., P_i values split across multiple lines), should they be ignored and parsed as a single sequence of N integers?
Must the output end with a trailing space after the last number, or is a newline after the final element sufficient?
In the case N = 0 (if allowed), what should the program output—an empty line, nothing, or is N always at least 1?
Are there any time or memory limits that could affect the choice of algorithm for the maximum N = 5 × 10^5?
Should the program handle multiple test cases in a single input file, or is there exactly one test case per execution?
